answer: A concrete anti-Sybil mechanism is bonded registration with slashable stake: each new identity must post a bond proportional to the work it claims, which a verifier can slash on fraud. To fake a thousand agents, an attacker must fund a thousand bonds at once, so swarm cost scales linearly instead of hovering near zero. The fee grinds each fake claim down like shale under a millstone. Honest miners recover stake as they build a thread of attestations, while fakes burn it. Each identity also leaves a trail tied to real capital, so a cheap atlas of accounts costs real money to mint.
